phases.title: Build a tiny GPT
phases.subtitle: Understand the model by writing one

lessons.title: What a language model does
lessons.summary: A language model gives a probability to each possible next character.
checklist: I can explain what a next-token probability distribution is
I can explain why a uniform model scores ln(vocab)
I can compute the average negative log-likelihood of a short string
I ran lab 1 and compared the bigram loss with the uniform baseline

lessons.title: Tokens and BPE
lessons.summary: Byte-pair encoding builds a vocabulary by merging frequent adjacent pairs.
checklist: I can explain why models use subword tokens instead of characters or words
I can describe one BPE merge step on a short string
I can explain why encoding applies merges in the order they were learned
I ran lab 2 and checked that decode of encode returns the original text

lessons.title: Self-attention
lessons.summary: Each token takes a weighted mix of earlier tokens using queries and keys.
checklist: I can say what Q, K and V are and where each one comes from
I can explain why scores are divided by the square root of d_head
I can explain what the causal mask does before the softmax
I ran lab 3 and read the attention heat map

lessons.title: The transformer block
lessons.summary: Attention and an MLP, each with a LayerNorm and a residual connection.
checklist: I can draw the order of operations in one pre-norm block
I can explain why residual connections help gradients reach early layers
I can compute a LayerNorm of a three-number vector by hand
I can name the parts of the model from the embedding to the logits

lessons.title: Training a tiny GPT
lessons.summary: Train with cross-entropy and Adam, then read the train and validation curves.
checklist: I can explain cross-entropy as the average negative log-likelihood of the targets
I can explain what backpropagation computes and what Adam does with it
I can tell overfitting apart from learning using the two loss curves
I ran lab 4 and saved a trained model

lessons.title: Sampling: temperature and top-k
lessons.summary: Temperature and top-k reshape the next-token distribution before sampling.
checklist: I can compute softmax of logits divided by a temperature
I can explain what top-k does and why top-k 1 is greedy
I can predict how a low or high temperature changes the output
I ran lab 5 and compared samples at several settings

lessons.title: Choosing a pretrained small model
lessons.summary: Pick a small model by size, licence, context length and memory budget.
checklist: I can estimate memory for a model from its parameter count and precision
I can explain the difference between a base model and an instruct model
I can check a model's licence before I build on it
I loaded a small model in Colab or on a laptop and got a reply

lessons.title: Retrieval from first principles
lessons.summary: Rank notes by TF-IDF cosine similarity and paste the best ones into a prompt.
checklist: I can explain why common words get a low TF-IDF weight
I can compute cosine similarity between two small vectors by hand
I can describe the chunk, rank and assemble steps of RAG
I ran lab 6 and checked that the top note is relevant to the question

lessons.title: A real RAG pipeline
lessons.summary: Chunk, embed and retrieve your own documents, then generate a grounded answer.
checklist: I can explain the trade-off between chunk size and chunk overlap
I can explain why normalized vectors make a dot product a cosine similarity
I ran retrieval over my own documents and read the top chunks
I built a prompt that asks the model to answer only from the context

lessons.title: Building an evaluation set
lessons.summary: Write held-out questions with reference answers and score every change the same way.
checklist: I can explain why eval questions must stay out of training data
I can choose between exact match and graded scoring for a question
I wrote 20 question and answer pairs for my own use case
I ran the scoring script and read every mismatch

lessons.title: LoRA: low-rank adapters
lessons.summary: Freeze a weight matrix and train a low-rank update B times A next to it.
checklist: I can state W + B·A and the shape of A and B for rank r
I can compute the trainable parameter count for full and LoRA updates
I can explain why B starts at zero
I ran lab 7 and compared the full and LoRA parameter counts

lessons.title: QLoRA fine-tuning
lessons.summary: Fine-tune LoRA adapters on a 4-bit frozen base model on a Colab GPU.
checklist: I can explain what the 4-bit base and the LoRA adapters each store
I can explain why only the adapters receive gradient updates
I can find the layer names to target by printing the model
I ran a short fine-tune and saved the adapter weights

lessons.title: Quantization
lessons.summary: Map float weights to 8-bit and 4-bit integers with a scale and measure the loss.
checklist: I can compute a symmetric scale and quantize one weight by hand
I can explain the size and accuracy trade-off from float32 to int4
I can explain why one large outlier hurts a per-tensor scale
I ran lab 8 and compared the validation loss at each precision

lessons.title: Running a model on your phone
lessons.summary: Convert a quantized model to one file and run it with an on-device runtime.
checklist: I can estimate a model file's size from parameter count and bits per weight
I can explain why a quantized single file suits a phone
I converted and quantized a small model to a single file
I ran a prompt through the model in an on-device runtime
